dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule and resultsSection.participantFlowModule: "Participants will receive guselkumab by subcutaneous injection with placebo as needed to maintain the blind." "Participants will receive placebo by subcutaneous injection then receive guselkumab by subcutaneous injection." "Guselkumab will be administered as subcutaneous injection." "Placebo will be administered as subcutaneous injection." "Participants received placebo matching to guselkumab by subcutaneous (SC) injection at Weeks 0, 4, and 12, and then crossed-over to receive guselkumab 100 milligrams (mg) as SC injection at Weeks 16, 20, 28, 36, and 44." "Participants received guselkumab 100 mg by SC injection at Weeks 0, 4 and then every 8 weeks (q8w) through Week 44." "Participants also received placebo at Week 16 to maintain the blind." "Group 1: Guselkumab" "Group 2: Placebo" "Guselkumab" "DRUG" -- Guselkumab is 100 mg SC in the registry result-arm descriptions. Group 1 receives guselkumab with placebo as needed to maintain blinding, while Group 2 receives placebo then crosses over to guselkumab at Week 16; the active arm also receives placebo at Week 16. Because the arm schedules differ and include an intervening placebo injection, no shared frequency or dosing_periods are assigned and co_administered_with is empty. Placebo is the matching comparator intervention. The two boolean placebo designations follow the registry intervention names and arm labels: Guselkumab is named as the active intervention, while Placebo is explicitly named as the matching comparator.

severity_criteria.source_excerpt: protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria and outcomesModule scale descriptions: "* All participants must meet the following disease severity criteria at screening and at baseline: (a) Overall Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) 3 (moderate) plaque psoriasis; (b) Body Surface Area (BSA) 2-15 percent (%) with at least 1 plaque outside of special sites; (c) Involvement of at least 1 special site with at least moderate severity." "Qualifying sites include scalp with scalp-specific IGA greater than or equal to (\>=) 3, face with facial psoriasis IGA \>=3, intertriginous with intertriginous psoriasis IGA \>=3, or genital with static physician global assessment of genitalia (sPGA-G) \>=3" "Final IGA score of psoriasis was based upon the average of induration, erythema and scaling scores assessed on a 5 point scale: cleared (0), minimal (1), mild (2), moderate (3), or severe (4)." "The ss-IGA instrument was used to evaluate the disease severity of scalp psoriasis." "The sPGA-G was a 6-point scale to assess the severity of genital psoriasis at a given time point." "The severity of genital psoriasis was assessed as clear (0), minimal (1), mild (2), moderate (3), severe (4), and very severe (5)." "The i-IGA was 5-point scale evaluating the severity of plaque psoriasis in the intertriginous area with scores defined as clear (0), minimal (1), mild (2), moderate (3), and severe (4)." "The f-IGA used a 5-point scale to assess overall facial disease severity, defined as clear (0), minimal (1), mild (2), moderate (3), and severe (4)." -- Eligibility requires the stated overall IGA and BSA thresholds and at least one qualifying special site. The four special-site thresholds are alternatives; they are represented as separate source criteria. The scale names are retained separately because the site instruments differ. The upper BSA bound 15 is copied from the printed interval 2-15 percent; it is not an independently printed numeric token.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: protocolSection.outcomesModule and resultsSection.participantFlowModule: "Percentage of Participants Who Achieved an Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) Score of Cleared (0) or Minimal (1) at Week 16" "Week 16" "Participants received placebo matching to guselkumab by subcutaneous (SC) injection at Weeks 0, 4, and 12, and then crossed-over to receive guselkumab 100 milligrams (mg) as SC injection at Weeks 16, 20, 28, 36, and 44." "Participants were then followed up for efficacy up to Week 48 and for safety up to Week 56." "Participants received guselkumab 100 mg by SC injection at Weeks 0, 4 and then every 8 weeks (q8w) through Week 44." "Participants also received placebo at Week 16 to maintain the blind." "Participants were then followed up for efficacy up to Week 48 and for safety up to Week 56." "Group 1: Placebo: From Week 0 to Week 16; Group 1: Placebo followed by Guselkumab 100 mg: From Week 16 to Week 56; Group 2: Guselkumab 100 mg: From Week 0 to Week 56" -- The registry identifies the primary outcome at Week 16. Its results narrative states the placebo-to-guselkumab crossover at Week 16 and injections through Week 44, followed by efficacy follow-up up to Week 48 and safety follow-up up to Week 56. Period entries preserve the Week 16 crossover; no end-of-treatment or follow-up start boundary is inferred from the last injection. The protocolSection time frame also gives arm-specific reporting intervals (placebo 0-16; placebo followed by guselkumab 16-56; guselkumab 0-56), which are outcome observation intervals, not proof that active treatment continued to Week 56. The cited CT.gov record contains narrative outcome timing, not a full per-visit schedule table.
